observable_outcome: A Lease reclaim no longer creates an orphan: Service.Claim's reclaim branch drives the superseded Execution to ExecutionLost in the same transaction that expires its Lease and issues the new one, guarded so no reclaim can ever fail because of it; the crashed attempt's late AcceptResult is still rejected, now by the outer optimistic-concurrency guard with domain.ErrStaleVersion, and a second probe at the current version proves the lease-expiry guard still rejects with domain.ErrLeaseExpired, so two independent guards are pinned where one was before.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Reproduce before fixing. With the code unchanged, drive a reclaim (claim, start, advance the injected clock past LeaseTTL, claim again) and assert that the superseded Execution is left non-terminal -- that is the orphan this task removes. Record the measured status and version. This reproduction must be a real executed check, not a description.

A2. Source change. In Service.Claim's reclaim branch (the inc.Status == domain.IncrementLeased path), inside the same s.mutate UnitOfWork closure that expires the Lease and saves the new Lease/Execution/Increment, read the superseded Execution with u.Execution(ctx, expiredLease.ExecutionID.String()), drive it through domain.MarkExecutionLost, and persist it with u.SaveExecution(ctx, next, exec.Version). Read and write it inside that closure only; no new UnitOfWork port and no store change is permitted.

A3. Guarded, never fatal to the reclaim. The termination happens only when the superseded Execution is found, is not already terminal, and its LeaseID/ExecutionID/FencingToken linkage matches the Lease being expired; otherwise it is skipped and the Claim proceeds unchanged. Add one test per skip branch -- Execution absent, Execution already terminal, linkage mismatch -- each asserting the Claim still succeeds and returns a usable new Lease/Execution. Prove the negative direction too: with the guard removed, the already-terminal case makes Claim fail (record the exact error), and with the guard restored it succeeds.

A4. Same-transaction atomicity. Assert that the termination and the reclaim are one unit: on a transaction that fails after the reclaim work, neither the new Lease nor the superseded Execution's terminal status is visible; on success both are. Assert the superseded Execution's Version advanced by exactly one and its FencingToken is retained.

A5. Positive invariant at the source. After a successful reclaiming Claim, assert directly that no non-terminal Execution exists behind an inactive Lease for that Increment -- the property that previously only OrphanSweep could eventually establish. Do not assert it by invoking the sweep.

A6. Crash journey, pinned error revised (this is the one authorised exception to keeping existing assertions unchanged; dp-v2-058 d2 is the ruling). In internal/runner/crash_test.go all three subtests of TestJourneyFourLocalCrashResumeAcrossExecutions keep their top-level test name, their subtest names and every other assertion, and change the late-accept expectation from errors.Is(lateErr, domain.ErrLeaseExpired) to errors.Is(lateErr, domain.ErrStaleVersion). A disjunction of the two error classes is prohibited. The test's doc comment must state, in prose, why the change does not weaken safety: that AcceptResult checks the expected Execution version before it calls domain.AcceptExecutionResult, that domain.MarkExecutionLost always advances the version, that the set of accepted submissions was empty before and is empty after, that no durable effect is constructed on either path, and that the rejection now happens earlier and further out rather than being relaxed.

A7. Coverage of the lease-expiry guard is not dropped. Each of the three subtests gains a second probe, with its own distinct RequestID so idempotency cannot short-circuit it: re-read the superseded Execution's current version (the existing executionSnapshot helper), submit AcceptResult with that current version and the crashed attempt's own lease and fencing token, and assert it is rejected with domain.ErrLeaseExpired. Keep the existing before/after equality assertion on the resumed Execution's canonical state around both probes, so neither rejected call moves canonical state. State in the evidence that this makes the journey pin two independent guards where it previously pinned one.

A8. Live suite pin, source-only. internal/runner/provider_live_test.go's testI5AndI6 late-accept pin is revised identically, and its doc comment is updated to match. Do not run the live suite and do not start any Provider CLI. Prove the change compiles (devbox run --pure -- go vet ./internal/runner and a test build of the package). Record this check with status skipped, never passed, and state in the evidence that V2-017's ev-v2-017-provider-live-claude record needs re-exercise before the next promotion, because internal/application/service.go changed.

A9. Nothing else changes. internal/domain is untouched. internal/reconciler, including orphan.go and the OrphanSweep tests, is untouched: the sweep still owns every orphan arising from an absent or revoked Lease or from a death with no reclaim. Assert that by running make component-reconciler unchanged and reporting that its tests still pass under the same names.

A10. Existing tests. Every other pre-existing test in internal/application and internal/runner still passes under its existing name with its assertions unchanged. Report the before and after top-level test counts for both packages, and name any test whose behaviour changed (only the three crash-journey subtests' late-accept expectation may appear).

A11. Determinism and race. No fixed sleep, no timer, no goroutine in the new tests; the reclaim is driven by advancing the injected clock. Run the two packages three times in sequence and record identical verdict lines, and run them once with -race.

A12. Evidence. Create two artifacts: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-058-application.json (id ev-v2-058-application, component application) and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-058-runner.json (id ev-v2-058-runner, component runner), both task_id V2-058, correlation_id v2-058-orphan-source. Each records for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout, and a summary stating the measured result; every acceptance item above is traceable to a named check. The A8 check is recorded with status skipped. A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). Register both with exactly two appended entries in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash values are the sha256 of each artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with both records in place.

A13. Each record's evidence_key is its own component key (application, runner) read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added -- a new file not yet added to the index is invisible to that key.
A14. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs.

A15. Record a staleness note naming which other active evidence records this change makes stale (at minimum ev-v2-016-runner, ev-v2-017-provider-live-claude and any record whose component depends on application), without editing any of them; V2-045's component re-issue resolves them under gate rule G6.
A16. No file outside allowed_paths changes. ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are untouched.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.
Do not touch ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*; the component dependency DAG and the toolchain surface are V2-045's task.
Do not touch .agents/v2/task-state/** or .agents/v2/packets/**; the coordinator records transitions and packets.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer, no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is expressed only as bounded deadline polling with an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.
A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with its status "skipped" and its reason.
Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment) in the evidence.
Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, stop and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating or weakening it.
Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex/claude/opencode) and do not touch any Google Cloud resource.

Keep the fail-closed direction unchanged: a stale submission from a superseded Execution must still be refused. Only the class of the refusal error may change, and only in the way dp-v2-058 d2 authorises.
Do not weaken the crash journey's assertion into a disjunction of two error classes, and do not delete the lease-expiry expectation; it moves to the second probe.
Do not reorder AcceptResult's expected-version check relative to the domain validation, and do not construct a terminal Execution without advancing its Version (dp-v2-058 d4).
Do not edit internal/domain and do not edit the OrphanSweep or its tests.
Do not run the live provider suite; the provider_live_test.go pin change is source-only and must be recorded as skipped, not passed.
Except for the three crash-journey subtests' late-accept expectation authorised by A6, every existing test keeps its name and its assertions.
